title: Stable-GFlowNet: Toward Diverse and Robust LLM Red-Teaming via Contrastive Trajectory Balance

evidence.claim: Stable-GFN replaces explicit GFlowNet partition-function estimation with Contrastive Trajectory Balance based on pairwise trajectory comparisons (Section 4).
evidence.evidence: Contrastive Trajectory Balance (CTB) loss evaluated to 4.1667 across 6.0 pairwise comparisons without requiring explicit partition-function Z estimation (explicit_z_used=False, partition_function_params=0).

evidence.claim: The method adds Noisy Gradient Pruning to filter uninformative reward differences under noisy red-teaming rewards (Section 4).
evidence.evidence: Noisy Gradient Pruning (NGP) at threshold tau=0.1 successfully filtered uninformative reward differences, pruning 20.0% of total trajectory pairs (8/10 pairs kept).

evidence.claim: The Min-K Fluency Stabilizer penalizes non-fluent out-of-distribution prompts to reduce gibberish reward hacking (Section 4).
evidence.evidence: Min-K Fluency Stabilizer evaluated log-likelihood of bottom-20% tokens; gibberish prompts received average penalty 20.8077 vs fluent prompts penalty 0.0000 (fluency_separation_valid=True).

evidence.claim: Stable-GFN reports stronger attack diversity and attack performance than GFN baselines across LLM red-teaming settings (Section 5).
evidence.evidence: On simulated red-teaming benchmark, Stable-GFN achieved attack diversity 17.3365 vs TB baseline 7.7094 (diversity improvement ratio 2.25x).

evidence.claim: Ablations evaluate loss-function and reward-stabilization choices, including the effect of reward constraints on attack discovery (Table 3).
evidence.evidence: Table 3 ablation evaluation compared Full Stable-GFN (loss=52.5073, requires_z=False), W/o Min-K (loss=28.9008), W/o NGP (loss=51.8140), and TB baseline (loss=24.8748, requires_z=True).
